source.document: Not a published curve: fitted by eye to the road closures at the 2023 Kahramanmaraş (M7.8) fault crossings
source.basis: A review of the Kahramanmaraş example: roads offset about 3 m sideways by the strike-slip rupture mostly stayed usable or were patched within hours; of the eight fault-crossing edges with a known outcome about 3 closed. A road offset with median about 3 m (sigma 0.3 ln) through this curve gives P(closed) about 0.3. The Hazus roadway curves (Table 7-5) treat about 1.5 m of any ground movement as closing a major road, which suits vertical movement, not a mostly horizontal offset.
source.calibration: One event, a handful of crossings: a rough fit, not a validated curve. Its outcomes are what it was fitted to, so they are no test of it.
source.window: Closed means not passable for relief traffic within the first 72 hours after the shock. KGM reopened every road closed on 6 February 2023 by 10 February, so on a one-week window almost no fault crossing would count as closed.
source.application: Every fault crossing, either road class (the evidence gives no difference between them). beta is the Hazus roadway beta, kept.
